assessor: RTS implementation preflight — Semantic Claim Refinement v1
rationale: Repository-local deterministic postprocessing of an already-valid I report only. J may add exact-anchor UNVERIFIED claim classifications from a controlled ontology and recompute review coverage. It does not fetch network data, call a model, modify raw source content, mutate H/F/G runtime behavior, or grant authority. Ambiguity, negation, truncation and ontology conflicts fail closed.
affected_boundaries: I report postprocessing and review-coverage audit
H bundle revalidation after added claims
focused DA and full A-J regression
existing_assumptions: I reports retain source content, exact claims and ambiguous anchor hashes.
H validate_bundle rejects malformed claim/bundle structures.
Docs claims remain UNVERIFIED and non-authorizing.

data_migration.notes: No existing intake report, transition report, profile, memory, FREEZER history or runtime configuration is mutated in place.

approval_changes: none; semantic refinement grants no execution/profile-application/promotion authority
review reduction is evidence-processing only and cannot apply H/F/G decisions
hidden_dependencies: semantic aliases must map only to H-supported areas and claim kinds
exact source anchors must remain unchanged
negative/exception language must never be auto-promoted as positive support
upstream ambiguous_findings_truncated prevents full READY state
original intake fingerprint must be preserved
rollback_boundary: Drop the J branch or revert semantic_claim_refinement files and FRZ-000020 append-only versions; A-I remain untouched.
completion_conditions: unique controlled semantic aliases can convert eligible ambiguous anchors into exact-anchor UNVERIFIED claims
upstream ambiguity truncation can never produce READY_FOR_H
existing lexical claims are not duplicated
A-J regressions and FREEZER verify pass
risks: v1 controlled aliases will reduce only a subset of real provider ambiguity
provider wording evolves and registry updates still require evidence-backed review
review count reduction is not itself correctness evidence
